meta.association: Heterozygous pathogenic variants disrupting BPTF cause an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder, with haploinsufficiency as the principal mechanism. Reported allele classes include frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, exon or whole-gene deletions, gene-disrupting rearrangements, in-frame deletions and missense substitutions. Clinical severity cannot be reliably predicted from allele class alone. The two missense variants in the 2025 four-person report were classified as variants of uncertain significance, so that series does not establish their pathogenicity or a missense-specific severe phenotype.

nodes.description: Bptf loss alters developmental gene expression in experimental systems. In conditional-null cortex, transcriptomic changes include neuronal fate regulators and stress-response pathways. MYC-binding-site enrichment is computational and does not demonstrate BPTF/MYC occupancy or a causal interaction in patient neurons. Postnatal bulk expression differences also reflect changed cell populations, including microglia. Embryonic stem-cell experiments additionally show context-dependent activation and repression of developmental genes and impaired Smad-responsive transcription despite preserved Smad2 phosphorylation. These findings are model-specific, not a demonstrated universal failure of upstream TGF-beta signaling.

nodes.description: BPTF is the chromatin-reader subunit of NURF, which can contain SMARCA1/SNF2L or SMARCA5/SNF2H. Its PHD finger recognizes H3K4me3 and its bromodomain recognizes acetylated histones. Biochemical evidence links histone recognition to NURF recruitment and remodeling. The 2006 recruitment experiment depleted H3K4me3 rather than modeling a heterozygous patient BPTF allele. Mouse genetic comparisons support different developmental roles and compensatory capacities of the NURF ATPases; direct NURF subunit exchange in human BPTF-haploinsufficient cortex remains unmeasured.

nodes.description: Human BPTF-related disease includes developmental delay, intellectual disability, speech/language delay, motor delay and hypotonia with variable expressivity. Developmental delay commonly precedes seizures, but this does not prove a specific cortical lesion or exclude additional developmental effects from epilepsy.

nodes.description: Two boys with short stature and growth hormone deficiency on stimulation testing received rhGH in the 2023 report. One gained 25.6 cm (+1.63 SD) over 3.5 years; the other gained 2.9 cm (+0.18 SD) over four months before treatment stopped for financial reasons. These uncontrolled observations do not establish long-term efficacy, safety or benefit in individuals without growth hormone deficiency.

nodes.description: Microcephaly in BPTF-related disease can be congenital or emerge after birth. Reduced larval head size after zebrafish bptf disruption and cortical hypoplasia in conditional-null mice support a developmental contribution, but the exact cellular route in human heterozygous disease is unresolved. Microcephaly and neurodevelopmental impairment may share upstream causes; reduced head size does not itself establish the cause of cognitive impairment.

nodes.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy for NEDDFL. Management is supportive and centres on early intervention: speech and language therapy (given the disproportionate speech delay), physical and occupational therapy for motor delay and hypotonia, educational support, nutritional support for poor weight gain and feeding difficulty, and periodic monitoring for scoliosis and ophthalmologic problems.
